title: Test When Added Planning Edges Help or Harm Agent Workflow Execution
target_platform: Shared orchestrating-agent-work skill (graph_runner.py, topology-rules.md, graph-planning.md) in companion repo richfrem/agent-plugins-skills
score_basis: Provisional estimates: Strategic leverage 4 (directly informs multi-agent DAG planning and topology optimization across all repository workflows), Epistemic depth 4 (tests whether Braess-like counter-intuitive inefficiencies exist in deterministic agent workflow DAGs), Cost weight 0.4 (evaluation relies primarily on deterministic local graph simulation and existing runner test fixtures; zero or minimal model calls), Operational friction 3 (requires inspecting companion repository execution model and formulating valid matched fixtures). Priority = (4 * 4) / (0.4 * 3) = 13.33.
hypothesis: Among at least 24 frozen matched workflow fixtures, adding the selected optional planning edge improves the declared local metric but worsens at least one predeclared end-to-end cost metric by 10% or more in at least 20% of fixtures, without changing task requirements.
falsification_criteria: Primary claim is FALSIFIED, with valid instruments and a completed held-out run, if fewer than 20% of frozen workflow fixtures satisfy both the local-benefit condition and the >=10% end-to-end cost increase condition. UNASSESSED (no verdict) if: Stage A finds no genuinely supported edge transformation in orchestrating-agent-work (reporting applicability not established rather than inventing an artificial executor); test fixtures are incomplete; instruments are invalid; or budget is exceeded. Missing measurements remain unknown.
strategic_intent: Investigate whether adding optional coordination or routing connections improves a local planning metric while worsening end-to-end execution. Use the existing skill's actual graph semantics and executor, rather than importing random-walk assumptions.
design_constraints: Identify and respect existing graph semantics: mandatory precedence/dependency edges, optional routing or delegation alternatives, feedback/retry transitions, and knowledge/context links.
Never remove required dependencies, authorization gates, validation scripts, or human review barriers to improve a metric.
Do not manufacture a new graph framework, scheduler, or Jev integration; use existing graph_runner.py and companion test harnesses.
Two-stage design: Stage A must establish genuine applicability in the actual codebase before freezing Stage B confirmatory fixtures.
Zero model calls for core graph topology checks; model calls are optional and require demonstrated necessity and approved budget.
If harmful cases are identified, any proposed guard must also be tested against beneficial shortcuts to ensure it does not indiscriminately block helpful edges.
Keep verdict null and status PROPOSED upon registration; registration does not authorize experiment execution.
experiment: Two-stage evaluation: Stage A inspects ../agent-plugins-skills/plugins/agent-orchestration/.apm/skills/orchestrating-agent-work/ references (graph-planning.md, graph-execution.md, topology-rules.md), implementation (scripts/graph_runner.py), and test fixtures (tests/test_graph_runner.py) to identify genuinely supported optional edge transformations (e.g. speculative read scatter or bypass). Stage B authors at least 24 matched workflow fixtures with identical deliverable requirements under deterministic execution parameters, freezes confirmatory protocols and evaluators, and measures end-to-end delivery success, total cost, makespan, and retries under baseline vs. edge-added variants.
measurement_requirements: Separate local planning metric changes from global end-to-end delivery metrics.
Measure accepted delivery rate, total execution cost/work, makespan/latency, and retry/waste counts.
Distinguish empirical workflow outcomes from synthetic random-walk analogies.
Report individual fixture outcomes separately; do not claim sample frequency estimates production prevalence.
agent_guidance: Do not execute experiment runs or edit companion skill files during registration.
Consult existing documentation and test fixtures rather than guessing graph_runner behavior.
If Stage A shows no supported optional transformation, report applicability failure rather than forcing an analogy.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Frontier models are not authorized for execution; local Python test harnesses and deterministic fixtures execute the evaluation.
